summary: Declare metric thresholds in KDL; the daemon evaluates conditions in the background and notifies owners once on breach and recovery.

replay.detail: No graph replay; one-time re-admission of old unknown-family invalid records per new schema digest. Local condition heads re-seed through bounded indexed seeks whenever declarations change. Membership changes also trigger indexed reconstruction, which resumes over multiple ticks; local tracker restoration reads its own indexed state directly.

schema.detail: Adds condition declarations and condition-instance/condition-hash/origin-hash/instance-hash subjects with authenticated system-only durable transitions. Storage version stays 18; four local cache tables and a desired-condition partial index are created on open, without a global claims-index build. Heads are keyed by declaration/origin/instance with local origin/phase/order indexes; disposable development caches with the older key rebuild on open.

rules.detail: condition.state is durable and never trimmed: no checkpoint rule changes. Only entry/recovery append; routine and hold phases stay local. At minimum holds plus cooldown, flapping can append about two claims per seven minutes (~411/day/instance), at most 32 declarations x eight local instances. This is a worst-case transition bound, not a steady-sample stream. At the full 32 x 8 local-instance bound this is about 105,000 claims/day/host, roughly 100–200 MB/day for typical 1–2 KB claims, replicated and retained on each member; maximum bounded identities/payloads can be larger. There is no daily byte quota.

compatibility.detail: Adds /v1/conditions and st conditions ls/show. Client-v0 adds condition attention kind; generated clients/digest change and stui renders these alerts. Deploy all daemons before facts, daemon before CLI, and clients before person-owned declarations. Old daemons mark condition intent.desired invalid (degraded envelope) and condition.state unknown; these heal once after upgrade without replication repair. Shared TypeScript Home includes condition cards; stui does not offer human resolution controls or manual-clear guidance for these self-clearing alerts.

downtime.detail: Ordinary daemon restart; breaches resume silently, holds restart. Evaluation and live file+WAL size sampling every 30 seconds; one disk worker with stale diagnostics. Physical daily growth is deferred to the shared SLO sampler adapter; no separate hourly ring.

manual.detail: Operations must deploy all fleet daemons before publishing the first conditions. Keep existing watches until real-host breach/recovery verification and operations approval. Publication caps subtract same-apply stops; out-of-band replicated over-cap declarations produce an explicit invalid-declaration diagnostic. Missing breached instances remain last-known breach until measured recovery; absence cannot prove recovery. Process PID enumeration is bounded and may miss processes beyond the cap. Background tasks stop when the daemon runtime shuts down; an uninterruptible kernel call may delay shutdown. More than eight filesystems fails strict doctor until explicit path declarations cover them; list/show does not display evaluator diagnostics. Clear heads are evicted first; capacity omissions or breach evictions are diagnosed. Keyed fleets reconstruct current members and prune departed ones; legacy discovery caps at 256 origin and 64 instance namespaces with diagnostics. Discovery resumes across ticks, with a one-second/128-origin budget checked between origins. Global heads remain capped at 256 per condition, so excessive simultaneous breaches need narrower declarations. Full conditions responses remain bounded at 8,192 instances; pagination is deferred. The declaration cap reports all remaining omitted declarations (count bounded to 1,024). Anchored reconstruction excludes unkeyed legacy peers, and departed members lose alerts without synthetic recovery. Capacity diagnostics keep up to eight causes until full reseed. Notifications materialize only the oldest 256 queued rows; the durable queue remains uncapped and fairness is within that window. Unexpected non-validation storage failures retain rows with diagnostics indefinitely.

recovery.detail: Roll forward after declarations exist. An older daemon cannot evaluate them. Unknown-family records rejected by old registries heal on an upgraded schema; other invalid records require normal replication repair. Notification storage failures retain rows, deterministic validation failures consume three attempts, partial successful deliveries remain visible, and discarded rows leave a diagnostic for one hour.
